items.stem:
A map is drawn to a scale of 1 : 50 000.
On the map, the distance between the villages of Aldbrook and Fenwick is 8 cm.

parts.t: Work out the actual distance between the two villages. Give your answer in kilometres.

ms:
M1 for 8 × 50 000 (= 400 000 cm) oe
A1 cao
allow M1 for 400 000 seen with no conversion
sols: A scale of 1 : 50 000 means 1 cm on the map represents 50 000 cm on the ground.
multiply the map distance by the scale factor

items.stem: A road atlas uses a scale of 1 : 200 000.

parts.t: Two petrol stations are 6.5 cm apart on the map. Work out the actual distance between them, in kilometres.

Complete this statement:
1 cm on the map represents …… km on the ground.

sols: convert the scale directly into kilometres

items.stem:
Priya draws a plan of her school hall.
She uses a scale of 1 cm to 4 m.

parts.t: The hall is 26 m long. Work out the length of the hall on the plan.
A door is 1.5 cm wide on the plan. Write down the actual width of the door.

sols: The scale is 1 cm to 4 m, so divide the real length by 4.
Multiply the plan length by 4 to get the real length.

items.stem:
A walking map has a scale of 1 : 25 000.
The straight track from the car park to the waterfall measures 5.6 cm on the map.

parts.t: Calculate the actual length of the track. Give your answer in kilometres.
Samira cycles along the whole track at an average speed of 12 km/h. Calculate the time she takes, in minutes.

ms:
M1 for their 1.4 ÷ 12 (= 0.11666… h) oe
A1 FT their (a)

items.stem: A map is drawn to a scale of 1 : 20 000.

parts.t: Show that an area of 1 cm<sup>2</sup> on the map represents an actual area of 4 × 10<sup>4</sup> m<sup>2</sup>.
A forest has an area of 12 cm<sup>2</sup> on the map. Calculate the actual area of the forest, in km<sup>2</sup>.

ms:
M1 for 20 0002 = 4 × 108 (cm2)
A1 for ÷ 10 000 leading to 4 × 104, nfww
sols: A length scale factor of 20 000 gives an area scale factor of 20 000<sup>2</sup>.
areas scale by the square of the length scale factor

items.stem: On a map, a straight canal of actual length 15 km is drawn 25 cm long.

parts.t: Find the scale of the map. Give your answer in the form 1 : n.
A railway line is 9 km long. Work out its length on this map.

ms:
M1 for 15 km = 1 500 000 cm soi
A1 cao, accept n = 60 000

M1 for 900 000 ÷ their 60 000 oe
A1 FT their (a)
sols: Write both lengths in the same unit.
write the ratio in the form 1 : n

items.stem: An architect makes a model of an office block using a scale of 1 : 150.

parts.t: The actual office block is 24 m tall. Calculate the height of the model, in centimetres.
One face of the model has an area of 6 cm<sup>2</sup>. Calculate the actual area of that face, in m<sup>2</sup>.

sols: work in a single unit before using the scale
The length scale factor is 150, so the area scale factor is 150<sup>2</sup> = 22 500.
areas scale by the square of the length scale factor

items.stem: Two towns are 12 cm apart on a map with a scale of 1 : 50 000.

parts.t: Calculate the actual distance between the two towns, in kilometres.

A second map of the same area has a scale of 1 : 20 000.
Work out the distance between the two towns on the second map.

ms:
M1 for 600 000 ÷ 20 000 oe or 12 × 50 000⁄20 000
A1 FT their (a)
sols: The actual distance does not change, only the scale does.
the second map has a smaller n, so it shows the same ground larger

items.stem: A scale model of a water tower is made using a scale of 1 : 250.

parts.t: The model is 92 cm tall. Calculate the height of the real water tower, in metres.
The model holds 32 cm<sup>3</sup> of water. Calculate the capacity of the real water tower, in m<sup>3</sup>.

ms:
M1 for 2503 (= 15 625 000) soi
M1 for 32 × their 15 625 000 (= 5 × 108 cm3)
A1 cao
sols: multiply the model length by the scale factor
The length scale factor is 250, so the volume scale factor is 250<sup>3</sup>.
volumes scale by the cube of the length scale factor

items.stem:
The diagram shows a triangular field ABC drawn on a map with a scale of 1 : 25 000.
On the map, AB = 4.8 cm, BC = 6.5 cm and angle ABC = 90°.

parts.t: Calculate the actual length of AC. Give your answer in kilometres, correct to 3 significant figures.
Calculate the actual area of the field. Give your answer in km<sup>2</sup>.

ms:
M1 for 1⁄2 × 4.8 × 6.5 (= 15.6 cm2)
M1 for × 25 0002 (= 9.75 × 109 cm2) oe
A1 cao
sols: Triangle ABC has a right angle at B, so use Pythagoras' theorem on the map lengths first.
the two perpendicular sides are the base and the height
areas scale by the square of the length scale factor
since 1 cm represents 0.25 km, 1 cm<sup>2</sup> represents 0.0625 km<sup>2</sup>

items.stem: A map of a country is drawn to a scale of 1 : 2 500 000.

parts.t: Two cities are 175 km apart. Calculate the distance between them on the map.

A second map is drawn to a scale of 1 : 25 000.
Write down which map shows the two cities further apart.

sols: On the 1 : 25 000 map, 1 cm represents only 250 m, so the same ground takes 100 times more paper.
The 1 : 25 000 map shows the cities further apart
the smaller the number n, the larger the scale
ms:
M1 for 175 × 100 000 ÷ 2 500 000 oe or 25 km per cm soi
A1 cao

items.stem: A hiking map uses a scale of 1 cm to 250 m.

parts.t: Write this scale in the form 1 : n.
A footpath is 4 km long. Work out its length on the map.

sols: Both parts of the ratio must be in the same unit, so write 250 m in centimetres.
4 km = 4000 m, and every 250 m is 1 cm on the map.

items.stem: A toy company makes a model of a car using a scale of 1 : 24.

parts.t: The real car is 4.32 m long. Calculate the length of the model, in centimetres.
A wheel on the model has diameter 2.5 cm. Work out the diameter of a wheel on the real car.

sols: the real car is 24 times larger than the model

items.stem:
In a nature book, a drawing of a beetle is 6 cm long.
The real beetle is 8 mm long.

parts.t: Find the scale of the drawing in the form n : 1.
The real beetle's wing is 4 mm long. Work out the length of the wing in the drawing, in centimetres.

sols: 6 cm = 60 mm, so the drawing is 60 : 8 compared with the real beetle.
an enlargement has the larger number first
ms:
M1 for 60 : 8 oe
A1 cao
1 : 7.5 scores M1 only

items.stem: On a plan drawn to a scale of 1 : 200, a rectangular vegetable garden measures 4.5 cm by 3 cm.

parts.t: Work out the actual length and width of the garden, in metres.
A fence is built around the whole garden. Work out the length of the fence.

sols: lengths scale by the same factor, so the plan perimeter 15 cm × 200 = 3000 cm also works

items.stem: A tourist map states its scale as “2 cm to 5 km”.

parts.t: Write the scale in the form 1 : n.
Two beaches are 7 cm apart on the map. Work out the actual distance between them.
A coast road is 30 km long. Work out its length on the map.

sols: 5 km = 500 000 cm, so the scale is 2 : 500 000.
2 cm represents 5 km, so 1 cm represents 2.5 km.
Every 2.5 km is 1 cm on the map.
ms:
M1 for 2 : 500 000 or 1 cm to 2.5 km soi
A1 cao

items.stem: A map has a scale of 1 : 50 000.

parts.t: Write down the actual distance, in kilometres, represented by 1 cm on the map.
A lake has an actual area of 6 km<sup>2</sup>. Calculate the area of the lake on the map.

sols: 1 cm represents 0.5 km, so 1 cm<sup>2</sup> represents 0.5<sup>2</sup> = 0.25 km<sup>2</sup>.
areas scale by the square of the length scale factor
divide the real area by the area of one square centimetre
ms:
M1 for 0.52 or 50 0002 soi
M1 for 6 ÷ their 0.25 oe
A1 cao

items.stem:
On a map with a scale of 1 : 10 000, a field has an area of 3 cm2.
1 hectare = 10 000 m2.

parts.t: Calculate the actual area of the field, in m<sup>2</sup>.
Write down the actual area of the field in hectares.
A second map has a scale of 1 : 5000. Calculate the area of the field on the second map.

sols: 1 cm represents 10 000 cm = 100 m, so 1 cm<sup>2</sup> represents 100<sup>2</sup> = 10 000 m<sup>2</sup>.
square the length scale factor for areas
The second map has half the value of n, so every length is twice as long on it.
Areas are 22 = 4 times as large: 3 × 4 = 12 cm2
ms:
M1 for length factor 2 or area factor 4 soi, or 30 000 ÷ 502
A1 FT

items.stem: Jonas cycles along a straight road for 45 minutes at an average speed of 16 km/h.

parts.t: Calculate the distance he cycles.
On a map with a scale of 1 : 200 000, work out the length of this road.

sols: speed is in km per hour, so use hours
ms:
M1 for their 12 × 100 000 ÷ 200 000 oe
A1 FT their (a)

items.stem:
An architect draws the plan of a rectangular classroom to a scale of 1 : 50.
On the plan the classroom measures 9 cm by 7 cm.

parts.t: Calculate the actual floor area of the classroom, in m<sup>2</sup>.
Carpet costs $24 per square metre. Work out the cost of carpeting the whole floor.

ms:
M1 for 9 × 50 or 7 × 50 (or 63 × 502)
M1 for 4.5 × 3.5 oe with consistent units
A1 cao

items.stem: A model of a sailing boat is made to a scale of 1 : 40.

parts.t: The mast of the real boat is 12 m tall. Work out the height of the mast on the model, in centimetres.
The deck of the real boat has an area of 60 m<sup>2</sup>. Calculate the area of the deck on the model, in cm<sup>2</sup>.

sols: areas scale by the square of the length factor
the model is smaller, so divide
ms:
M1 for 402 = 1600 soi
M1 for 60 ÷ 1600 oe or 600 000 ÷ 1600
A1 cao

items.stem:
A model of a swimming pool is made to a scale of 1 : 50.
1 m3 = 1000 litres.

parts.t: The real pool is 25 m long. Write down the length of the model pool, in centimetres.
The real pool holds 2 500 000 litres of water. Calculate the number of litres the model pool holds.

sols: volumes scale by the cube of the length factor
ms:
M1 for 503 = 125 000 soi
M1 for 2 500 000 ÷ 125 000 oe
A1 cao

items.stem: On a map with a scale of 1 : 50 000, the length of a straight path is measured as 6.4 cm, correct to the nearest millimetre.

parts.t: Write down the lower bound and the upper bound of the measured length.
Calculate the upper bound of the actual length of the path, in kilometres.
Amara walks the path at 4.5 km/h. Using the upper bound of the actual length, calculate the greatest time she could take, in minutes.

sols: Nearest millimetre = nearest 0.1 cm, so the maximum error is half of 0.1 cm = 0.05 cm.
Lower bound = 6.4 − 0.05 = 6.35 cm; upper bound = 6.4 + 0.05 = 6.45 cm
Upper bound of actual length = 6.45 × 50 000 = 322 500 cm
use the upper bound of the measurement
greatest distance at the fixed speed gives the greatest time
ms:
M1 for their 6.45 × 50 000 oe
A1 FT their upper bound

items.stem:
The diagram shows a field ABCD drawn on a map with a scale of 1 : 20 000.
AB is parallel to DC, angle DAB = 90°, AB = 5.5 cm, DC = 3.5 cm and AD = 4 cm.
1 hectare = 10 000 m2.

parts.t: Calculate the actual area of the field, in hectares.
Calculate the actual length of the side BC. Give your answer to the nearest metre.

sols: area of a trapezium = <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub>(sum of parallel sides) × height
1 cm represents 20 000 cm = 200 m, so 1 cm<sup>2</sup> represents 200<sup>2</sup> = 40 000 m<sup>2</sup>.
areas scale by the square of the length factor
Drop the perpendicular from C to AB: it makes a right-angled triangle with legs 5.5 − 3.5 = 2 cm and 4 cm.
the difference of the parallel sides and the height
ms:
M1 for 1⁄2(5.5 + 3.5) × 4 (= 18)
M1 for 2002 or 20 0002 soi
M1 for their 18 × 40 000 (= 720 000 m2) oe
A1 cao

items.stem:
On a map, a rectangular reservoir measures 2.4 cm by 1.5 cm.
The actual area of the reservoir is 0.9 km2.

parts.t: Find the scale of the map in the form 1 : n.
Work out the actual length of the reservoir, in kilometres.

sols: the length factor is the square root of the area factor
check: 2.4 cm → 1.2 km and 1.5 cm → 0.75 km; 1.2 × 0.75 = 0.9 km<sup>2</sup> ✓
ms:
M1 for 2.4 × 1.5 (= 3.6)
M1 for 0.9 km2 = 9 × 109 cm2 oe
M1 for √(their area ratio)
A1 cao
